# the contributor audit: robust inner-triangle closure by cap contraction

Source: `candidate 3a87cc28ce06445f`,
in its current strengthened version. Verdict: PASS.

With B nonheavy, the original two cap profiles and a hypothetical bad
target give `F<=a`, so the residual intersection has area at least
`w/4>0`. Its shared point forces the largest cap's maximum height
`h>2`. This conclusion concerns the original cuts, before any shift.

The original A cap has actual height `H=h+1>3`. Contracting that cap
toward a highest point by factor `1-eta/H` stays in A and raises its
lowest level by eta. The shifted captured area is therefore at least
`(1-eta/H)^2 w`, and hence at least `(1-eta/3)^2 w`.

The facet of the actual inner triangle lies in B, even if the outer
supporting facet is short. Its midpoint sum with the shifted A cap
lies in the original unshifted K cap. Exact planar segment addition
then gives the displayed lower bound on Q. Subtracting the bad-profile
upper bound leaves a positive coefficient of w plus
`1/4-3 eta+3 eta^2/4`. This constant is nonnegative through
`eta*=2-sqrt(33)/3`; the positive w term proves strict contradiction
even at that endpoint. At eta one twelfth the constant is one 192nd.

The missing-volume conversion is independent of facet continuity:
every point of the inner homothet is the centroid of an eta-scaled
copy of the original body lying inside it. Separation and ordinary
Grunbaum then force at least `Gamma_d eta^d` missing relative volume
if that point were outside B. The planar simple threshold is exactly
one 324th at eta one twelfth.

No global-maximizer premise, diameter estimate, or tilt equalization
is needed in this strengthened proof. If B is heavy its own centroid
supplies OC separately; the strict source-depth conclusion is stated
only in the nonheavy branch. The full criticality hypothesis still
ensures that Q controls every actual ambient halfspace, not just the
three displayed caps.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
